summary.text: Subject 1 is a child (gender M) with a surgical indication for a cochlear implant (CI), bilateral, congenital, severe and/or profound SNHL and a compound heterozygous CDH23 genotype listed as etiology. Table 1 lists 6 months of sensorial deprivation, 12 months of hearing aid use before the CI, CI activation at 20 months (Med-El, left side) and effective CI use. The child used bimodal stimulation, attended speech-language-hearing therapy at least once a week and had no neurologic or cognitive impairment.

Each study-group child was assessed at four moments, before CI activation and after three months, nine months and five years of CI use, with long-latency auditory evoked potentials and behavioral protocols. No electrophysiological response was present before the CI, the P1 component was present after three months, and P1 latency decreased from the third to the ninth month. On the GASP the auditory skill level was Detection at 9 months and Comprehension at 5 years.

The child had effective CI use (Table 1). The methods say 'IC users' underwent periodic follow-up at the cochlear implant group without saying all of them, so that statement stays review-only for this child. The abstract says five children with effective CI use had decrease or stabilization of P1 latency and gradual development of auditory and oral language skills, but neither finding is individually specified for this child, so both stay review-only.

summary.text: Subject 2 is a child (gender F) with a surgical indication for a cochlear implant (CI), bilateral, congenital, severe and/or profound SNHL and a homozygous GJB2 c.35delG mutation listed as etiology. Table 1 lists 9 months of sensorial deprivation, 21 months of hearing aid use before the CI, CI activation at 31 months (Neurelec, right side) and effective CI use. The child used bimodal stimulation, attended speech-language-hearing therapy at least once a week and had no neurologic or cognitive impairment.

Each study-group child was assessed at four moments, before CI activation and after three months, nine months and five years of CI use, with long-latency auditory evoked potentials and behavioral protocols. No electrophysiological response was present before the CI, the P1 component was present after three months, and P1 latency decreased from the third to the ninth month. On the GASP the auditory skill level was Detection at 9 months and Comprehension at 5 years.

The child had effective CI use (Table 1). The methods say 'IC users' underwent periodic follow-up at the cochlear implant group without saying all of them, so that statement stays review-only for this child. The abstract says five children with effective CI use had decrease or stabilization of P1 latency and gradual development of auditory and oral language skills, but neither finding is individually specified for this child, so both stay review-only.

summary.text: Subject 6 is a child (gender F) with a surgical indication for a cochlear implant (CI), bilateral, congenital, severe and/or profound SNHL and an etiology recorded as 'Genetic to clarify'. Table 1 lists 12 months of sensorial deprivation, 9 months of hearing aid use before the CI, CI activation at 21 months (Cochlear Corporation, right side) and no effective CI use. The child used bimodal stimulation, attended speech-language-hearing therapy at least once a week and had no neurologic or cognitive impairment.

Each study-group child was assessed at four moments, before CI activation and after three months, nine months and five years of CI use, with long-latency auditory evoked potentials and behavioral protocols. No electrophysiological response was present before the CI, the P1 component was present after three months, and P1 latency decreased from the third to the ninth month. On the GASP the auditory skill level was Detection at 9 months and Detection at 5 years. P1 latency increased after five years of CI use.

Effective CI use stopped: the abstract places this after the first year of activation, whereas Results place it after nine months, a source conflict. Up to the ninth month the child consistently used the CI with orality as the main means of communication; after five years Brazilian Sign Language was the main means. Auditory and oral language performance worsened after about five years, including IT-MAIS/MAIS results, and the authors link this to stopping effective use. The methods say 'IC users' underwent periodic follow-up at the CI group without saying all of them, so that statement stays review-only for this child.

summary.text: Subject 7 is a child (gender M) with a surgical indication for a cochlear implant (CI), bilateral, congenital, severe and/or profound SNHL and Usher syndrome listed as etiology. Table 1 lists 18 months of sensorial deprivation, 36 months of hearing aid use before the CI, CI activation at 54 months (Neurelec, right side) and no effective CI use. The child used bimodal stimulation, attended speech-language-hearing therapy at least once a week and had no neurologic or cognitive impairment.

Each study-group child was assessed at four moments, before CI activation and after three months, nine months and five years of CI use, with long-latency auditory evoked potentials and behavioral protocols. No electrophysiological response was present before the CI, the P1 component was present after three months, and P1 latency decreased from the third to the ninth month. On the GASP the auditory skill level was Detection at 9 months and Detection at 5 years. P1 latency increased after five years of CI use.

Effective CI use stopped: the abstract places this after the first year of activation, whereas Results place it after nine months, a source conflict. Up to the ninth month the child consistently used the CI with orality as the main means of communication; after five years Brazilian Sign Language was the main means. Auditory and oral language performance worsened after about five years, including IT-MAIS/MAIS results, and the authors link this to stopping effective use. The methods say 'IC users' underwent periodic follow-up at the CI group without saying all of them, so that statement stays review-only for this child.

article_limitations: The seven normal-hearing control-group children are described only as a group (mean and range of age, audiometric criteria); they are not individually described and are not rostered.

Individual P1 latencies, IT-MAIS/MAIS and MUSS percentages, word-list percentages and correlation statistics are printed or plotted only inside figures (pixel content): recorded in visual.json, not as facts. Table 2 values are group means and are not copied to individuals.

Unlabelled counts of children are not assigned to individuals: one child at the maximum IT-MAIS/MAIS value at nine months, three children with lower MUSS scores, three children with word-list data, two children with maximum auditory performance and one with maximum oral language performance.
Source conflict: the abstract says children 6 and 7 stopped effective CI use after the first year of activation while Results say after nine months; both timings are kept review-only.

Aggregate mean values in the study-group description (sensory deprivation one year and six months; hearing aid use one year and nine months) are not the arithmetic means of the Table 1 columns; individual Table 1 values are kept literally and the aggregate means are not copied.

The Discussion uses 'maximum auditory skills (comprehension)' for three children and 'maximum auditory performance' for two children without naming a measure for the second count; the three-child count is mapped to subjects 1, 2 and 5 only as a review-only fact and the two-child count is not assigned.
Table 3 column headers read '9 months' and '5 years' without stating the reference point; the methods say after nine months of CI use.
Table 2 footnote marks significance with a hash but the table cells use an asterisk (print artefact, aggregate only).
Roster: reported count seven is the study group; the seven control children are aggregate-only and not counted as individually described patients.
Subjects 6 and 7 are first named in Results (b00026), before the Table 1 rows; patients are numbered by the Table 1 subject numbers and their identity evidence is the Table 1 row.
The Authors' Contributions paragraph (b00052) names people who are not in the article's author list; it is administrative, not clinical, and is not used.
